title.narrative: GPE Supporting LEG Coordination and Capacity building to develop Sudan Transitional Education Plan 2025-27

description.narrative:
This Element is dedicated to the GPE fund.
I. Context: The conflict that erupted on 15 April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) continues to inflict dire consequences on civilians, exacerbating the protracted economic troubles and pre-existing conflicts in the country. Thousands of people were killed and injured, millions of people fleeing their homes in search of safety, both inside Sudan and across its borders, and millions grappling with a lack of access to food, water, and other basic services. OCHA reported that since the start of the conflict, the magnitude of IDPs and refugees is on the rise - over 1 million people were forced to cross into neighboring countries and more than 4.2 million people (845,779 Households) have been displaced to (3,929) locations across all 18 states. Approximately 25 million people, roughly half of Sudan’s population, are now vulnerable and need humanitarian assistance and protection through the end of 2023 . An estimated 19 million children in Sudan are out of school, some 6.5 million lost access to school due to the conflict, and 10,400 schools shuttered in conflict-affected areas , and 171 schools are serving as emergency shelters for the displaced population , exposing children to dangers including recruitment into armed groups, and sexual violence. The number of displaced, separated, or unaccompanied children will continue to increase as families flee. This emphasizes the need to support education to ensure its continuity and ensure that Sudanese children equitably access school and have sufficient psychosocial support in safe and child-friendly learning spaces. This calls for not only coordinated action at the national level but also a harmonized approach at the regional level. The Minister of Education (MoE) recently issued a directive for the resumption of all academic activities in all government, private, and non-governmental schools, and higher education institutions where security conditions permit, following months’ full closure of education institutions throughout the country. As requested by the MoE to support school reopening, education partners, including UNESCO, are seeking ways to ensure access and equity to safe education, and alternative learning options for learners, especially IDPs, to mitigate learning deficits and ensure continuity of learning. A key member of the Local Education Group (LEG) in Sudan, UNESCO Khartoum leads critical education portfolios and works closely with key national stakeholders as well as development and humanitarian partners to make sure learning continues under all circumstances. In addition to leading technical fields, UNESCO has recently taken on board the role of LEG Coordinating Agency in the framework of GPE, whereby the organization has been entrusted with strengthening the coordination of education actors through the identification of emergency priorities and harmonizing donor financing around them. In the last meeting of the LEG, held on November 27, 2023, it was agreed among members to develop a Transitional Education Plan for the period 2024 to 2026 (TEP 2024-26).
II. Principles: For the process of TEP development to be meaningful and achieve its objectives, a series of principles need to be followed: LEG-led: The educational plan is considered a LEG instrument and a common framework for partner activities and activities supported by the national and state-level Ministry of Education with the participation of development and humanitarian partners. It is also considered a means of adapting to the emergency and early recovery of educational activities by identifying strategies that address the direct and urgent needs of the education sector. Therefore, the responsibility for its success depends on the participation of all concerned. While the planned interventions will require close cooperation between international and education experts, it will be necessary to ensure The Ministry of Education remains in consultation throughout the educational development process. Participatory: The plan is developed through a fully participatory process, to ensure that all LEG members and relevant ministries are consulted and engaged with all stakeholders (such as education partners, civil society, teachers’ unions, development and implementation partners, and humanitarian partners) and their views are considered. Transparency & mutual accountability: Transparency and mutual accountability are a central issue that is enhanced through the distribution of roles and responsibilities among key supporters and the efficient use of available resources. Transparency increases the ability of partners to hold each other accountable for their commitments, which improves performance and ensures successful implementation. Well-organized: The participatory planning process requires that it be well-organized and supported clearly by an organizational structure for the plan preparation process, and detailed clarification on the roles and responsibilities of the actors, especially the actors who lead and coordinate the process. III. TEP development governance structure: (To be agreed upon later) Led by the LEG, Organized and managed by the CA, UNESCO. 2 International experts, provided by UNESCO. 1 National expert, provided by UNESCO. 1 International expert, provided by UNHCR. IV. Scope of Work: TEP development in main steps: The Transitional Education Plan will identify strategic priorities and key educational objectives over the coming years (2024-2026). An approach will be adopted to ensure that the basic and urgent educational needs of all learners in Sudan, including girls, boys, and children with disabilities, are met. Attention will also be paid to gender issues, the social support program, humanitarian needs, peacebuilding, and development needs, to respond appropriately to the emergency while considering emerging needs. The plan will be developed through a series of steps detailed below, each step of which corresponds to a chapter of the final TEP document. Determining the implementation cost implications and expected financial constraints will also require back-and-forth adjustments until a practical and feasible mix of strategic programs and objectives are agreed upon by all partners and stakeholders. Phase 0: Preparation and roadmap development This phase consists of mobilization and consultations with the Ministry of Education, development and humanitarian partners, and education experts to agree on the structure of the process and develop the terms of reference, conceptual details, detailed roadmap, checklist of data needs, workshops schedule, and roles and responsibilities and the organizational structure. Phase 1: Education situation analysis This phase will be done by reviewing documents, evidence, and indicators to determine the capabilities and performance of the education system at a specific time (Baseline will be agreed upon later) and the external factors that directly affected the continuity of the education performance. It will also include the analysis of the impact of the conflict on education, macroeconomic status, demographic and educational data, human resources data, displaced and refugee data, and gender-related issues, and identify enabling factors, and challenges while highlighting potential directions and priorities for the next phase. Phase 2: Design priorities and key strategies. This phase consists of identifying and ranking immediate and urgent priorities, based on consultations and challenges identified through consulting meetings and workshops as well as from existing national policies and international commitments, operational capabilities, and available resources. They will be formulated as priorities and main strategies that will contribute to the continuity of education in emergencies and pave the way for long-term goals, after they are agreed upon by LEG members to be included within the TEP. Phase 3: Strategic program and activity Design. Once the priorities, Key strategies, and objectives are agreed upon, specific strategic programs are designed to achieve the objectives. These programs include an indication of the specific objectives, indicators, and expected outputs, specifying the size of the required inputs, and the main activities that must be completed while clarifying the most important issues, which are the roles and responsibilities of the parties concerned in each activity. Phase 4: Plan costing and financing framework. This phase includes developing a cost and financing framework to ensure that funds and resources are appropriately allocated and available for all planned activities. More specifically, financial costing and models will be used, and a financial simulation model will be developed to help achieve an optimal scenario with any financial gap. Phase 5: implementation framework To activate the plan, it will be translated into an operational plan throughout the implementation of TEP 2024-2026, Identify the risks of TEP implementation, address the obstacles and weaknesses of the key capacity, and propose a capacity development to be adopted to support the implementation. Phase 6: Design the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Framework (MEL) In this phase, it is ensured that the plan is moving in the right direction to achieve its goals before, during, and after implementation while ensuring regular monitoring at its various levels according to evidence that includes all stages and levels. For this purpose, a MEL framework will be developed that includes a matrix for presenting monitoring and evaluation results, and a matrix for clarifying key performance indicators (KPIs); In addition to details of the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) framework.
V. TEP 2024-2026 development modalities and timeline: Working modalities: National/states consultations In line with the principles identified above, the development of the Transitional Education Plan will rely largely on working sessions, consultations, and technical discussions via face-to-face meetings (workshops to discuss the different stages/steps of work), in addition to an indispensable series of consultations with the GPE/focal point and national experts. Some technical workshops may be held outside Sudan (described below) and will include stakeholders, donors, development and humanitarian partners, and representatives of civil society organizations, in addition to consultations at the level of all states of Sudan. Clear instructions and tools will be developed to collect the required data and information and determine the urgent priorities, which will be distributed to the groups of participants before their participation in the consultation workshops to give them sufficient time to prepare their responses. To achieve that, (4) consultative meetings at the level of partners and stakeholders are envisaged, and (3) consultative meetings at the national and state levels (Detailed activities are shown in Annex A) Remote support and workshops outside of Sudan A significant amount of support will be provided between remote and face-to-face consultations and workshops, to ensure continued progress in identifying priorities and developing TEP document, it is proposed to conduct two workshops outside Sudan as follows: - A 3-day workshop to formulate and endorse the design, strategic programs and planning for the TEP based on the priorities identified. - A one-day workshop to endorse the complete TEP document In addition to the consultative meetings with the local education group, the number of which is 4 divided into the phases of work. Timeline: After enriching and discussing the draft document and integrating all notes, a validated draft of TEP will be available by the end of April 2024, to be submitted to GPE, organize a donor conference, and mobilize resources and support. Under the proposed timeline, TEP will be developed over a 3 to 5 months period starting December 2023 and ending in April 2024. However, it is recognized that unpredictable situations could affect the ability of some tasks to be carried out throughout the consultancy. A draft of TEP priorities will be available by February 2024, which means the rest of the time will mainly be related to the appraisal and endorsement process and finalizing the implementation and monitoring frameworks. Results Framework for this project:
Outcome 1: Sudan Education System Enhanced in planning and monitoring in Emergencies.
Output 1: Sudan has developed a Transitional Education Plan for 2024 - 26 in close consultation with LEG members. Activity 1: International and National experts are identified and recruited for the development of the TEP 2024 - 26. Activity 2: TEP 2024 -26 is well discussed and approved by members of the LEG. Activity 3: Studies informing the TEP 2024 - 26 are conducted and results are shared and approved among LEG partners.
Implementation Strategy:
UNESCO Khartoum will identify 2 International experts and 2 national experts to work together to develop the TEP 2024 – 26. The national experts will be one for the consultation with the LEG members and the second one will be for the consultation with national officials and NGOs. The 2 international experts will be with similar experience to Sudan education crises TEP development skills. These experts will be selected in close consultation with the UNESCO HQ, EiE and LEG members. 2 workshops will be conducted at various stages of the TEP 2024-26 development process, these consultation workshops will work on reaching agreement between the LEG members on priorities, strategy framework and it’s validation. The capacities of the LEG members will be developed through international experts in planning and monitoring of TEP 2024-26 as well as through UNESCO HQ and IEEP experts in the field.
